scope_note: Complete NCISM-aligned student study layer for Dinacharya Adhyaya: Sanskrit verses 1-48, verse-wise original explanations, conceptual organization, exam preparation and revision support. Historical practices and culturally specific instructions are contextualized rather than presented as modern medical advice.
learning_outcomes: Define Dinacharya and explain its place in Swasthavritta.
Explain the classical sequence of morning regimen from Pratarutthana through Dantadhavana, Anjana and related practices.
Describe Abhyanga, its classical benefits, special sites and contraindications.
Explain Vyayama, its benefits, appropriate dose, seasonal variation and hazards of over-exertion.
Explain Udvartana and Snana with their classical indications and precautions.
Enumerate and explain the ten harmful actions described in the Sadvritta section.
Explain the principles of appropriate speech, social conduct, sensory moderation, personal hygiene and environmental safety.
Explain the fivefold summary of Sadvritta and the role of daily self-review.
Distinguish historical classical prescriptions from modern clinical and public-health practice.

sections.title: 1. Pratarutthana and Dantadhavana (Verses 1-4)
content: Brahma Muhurta and the classical purpose of beginning the day with disciplined routine.
Classical tooth-cleaning materials, taste profile, twig dimensions and technique.
Contraindications to mechanical tooth-cleaning in specified clinical conditions.

sections.title: 2. Anjana, Navana, Gandusha, Dhuma and Tambula (Verses 5-7)
content: Classical eye-care concepts and the role of Sauviranjana and Rasanjana.
Sequence of morning head and sense-organ practices.
Tambula and its classical contraindications; distinction from modern tobacco-containing products.

sections.title: 3. Abhyanga (Verses 8-9)
content: Daily oil massage and its classical benefits.
Special importance of head, ears and feet.
Contraindications and situations requiring modification.

sections.title: 4. Vyayama and Udvartana (Verses 10-15)
content: Benefits of exercise.
Half-strength principle and seasonal variation.
Contraindications and hazards of over-exercise.
Udvartana and its classical effects on kapha, medas, body firmness and skin.

sections.title: 5. Snana (Verses 16-18)
content: Benefits of bathing.
Classical distinction between warm-water use for body and head.
Situations in which bathing is contraindicated or should be modified.

sections.title: 6. Sadvritta: Foundations (Verses 19-25)
content: Food after digestion and management of natural urges.
Dharma as the ethical foundation of happiness.
Kalyana-mitra and avoidance of harmful company.
Ten harmful actions of body, speech and mind.
Compassion, respect, helpfulness and equanimity.

sections.title: 7. Sadvritta: Speech, Social, Environmental and Personal Conduct (Verses 26-44)
content: Qualities of appropriate speech.
Moderation in trust and social interaction.
Sense restraint and the middle path.
Personal cleanliness, dress and travel safety.
Environmental hazards, posture, rest and historically contextualized social prescriptions.

sections.title: 8. Integration, Sadvritta Summary and Phala-shruti (Verses 45-48)
content: Learning from the world through critical observation.
Five-fold summary of Sadvritta.
Daily self-review through Sannihita-smriti.
Traditional fruits and conclusion of the chapter.

exam_focus: Dantadhavana: suitable classical materials, characteristics and contraindications.
Anjana, Rasanjana, Navana, Gandusha, Dhuma and Tambula.
Abhyanga: benefits, special sites and contraindications.
Vyayama: benefits, half-strength principle, seasonal variation, contraindications and complications of excess.
Udvartana and Snana: benefits and contraindications.
Ten harmful actions (papa karma) of body, speech and mind in verses 21-22.
Qualities of appropriate speech in verse 26.
Moderation of senses and Trivarga in verses 29-30.
Personal hygiene, travel and environmental safety teachings in verses 31-44.
Fivefold summary of Sadvritta in verse 46 and daily review in verse 47.

text_sources: Ayana Ayurveda classical text with commentarial material
source_text.verification_note: Verse numbering and chapter scope verified against the available source-text pages. Student meanings in AaptaKosha are original explanatory summaries and are not copied translations.

must_memorize: Anjana-related practices and their classical purpose
Abhyanga benefits, special sites and contraindications

long_answer: Explain Dinacharya according to Ashtanga Hridaya with special reference to Pratarutthana, Dantadhavana, Anjana, Abhyanga, Vyayama, Udvartana and Snana.
Describe Abhyanga and Vyayama with their benefits, indications/contraindications and appropriate use.
Explain the concept of Sadvritta and discuss the ten harmful actions described in verses 21-22.
Describe the principles of speech, social conduct, sensory moderation and personal hygiene taught in Dinacharya Adhyaya.
Explain the fivefold summary of Sadvritta and the role of Sannihita-smriti.
short_answer: Name the special sites of Abhyanga.
What are the benefits of Vyayama?
Enumerate the ten harmful actions of verses 21-22.
State the qualities of appropriate speech in verse 26.
viva: Why is Dinacharya placed immediately after Ayushkamiya?
What is the classical rationale for waking at Brahma Muhurta?
Why are head, ears and feet emphasized in Abhyanga?
What is the half-strength principle of Vyayama?
What does Sadvritta add to physical daily regimen?
What is the practical meaning of Sannihita-smriti?

revision_summary: Dinacharya integrates physical hygiene, exercise, bathing and behavioural discipline.
Verses 1-18 establish the bodily daily regimen.
Verses 19-44 expand the concept into Sadvritta: food discipline, ethical conduct, speech, relationships, hygiene and safety.
Verse 46 compresses Sadvritta into five principles; verse 47 adds daily self-review.
Verse 48 gives the traditional phala-shruti and closes the chapter.
